data.narrative:
Realta Fusion is a Series A–stage nuclear energy company that has raised $36M+ to date. The valuation universe comprises 11 comparables across public and private markets: 3 public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private-stage peers including Fuse Energy, X-Energy, and Nano Nuclear Energy. These companies span similar technology verticals within advanced nuclear but vary materially in stage, geography, and technical approach.

The peer-median method is inapplicable due to insufficient narrow-stage clustering; the private comp set lacks three or more direct same-stage peers with comparable valuation tiers needed for reliable cross-sectional analysis. The stage-progression method is therefore the primary triangulation vehicle. Using total raised ($36M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A-to-next-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $72M. A ±15% sensitivity band around this point estimate produces a low of $61M and high of $83M.

The analysis supports a median valuation of $72M, with a plausible range of $61M–$83M. Key uncertainties include the appropriate stage-progression multiplier in a capital-intensive, long-development-cycle sector where median step-ups may differ from venture norms; the absence of tight comparables limits conviction in the 2.0x assumption. Additional valuation revision risk stems from technology validation milestones and regulatory pathway clarity.
